comment: §3.6 already provides shared data exchange — distributed mediation, eventing, a participant registry — and we support it. What no component owns is following a commitment through: tracking whether a referral was actioned, noticing the follow-up that never happens, closing the loop. §3.6.1 lists "orchestrating a multi-step transaction" among the mediation functions, but that routes one exchange in flight — not a commitment's lifecycle across time: a referral (accepted → attended → outcome, or the follow-up that never comes) or a claim (eligibility → pre-auth → settlement, or the claim that stalls). Goal 3 asks for exactly this ("coordinate care over time… while tracking adherence and quality"), but the draft folds it into the CDSE and into "care-coordination and referral tools" outside DPI-H. We recommend recognising this as a shared capability, distinct from decision support. The §2.1.1 test for shared infrastructure — reusable, stable interface, no lock-in, foundational not programme-specific — is met by it. We mean the shared exchange between systems — not every consuming application (an EMR or a payroll system is rightly application-layer). (On whether such a capability may be transactional, see C2.) It makes breaks in continuity visible; it does not assume the digital layer can resolve the underlying service-delivery constraint — a vacancy, or a lack of capacity — and it should be designed for real conditions: intermittent connectivity, workforce gaps, weak supervision, and incomplete facility-capability information.
